points.text: Software description with no new method or insight; weak ICLR fit, no adoption evidence
Generality claim untested; only Gemma3-4B with BTX, no compatibility matrix
Regex rewriting and copying modeling files is brittle
BTS and Traditional MoE never evaluated
No check that implementations reproduce published BTX/BTS behaviour
No expert utilisation or routing-entropy statistics; no load-balancing alpha ablation
Claimed reproduction of Shang et al. lacks original numbers for comparison
Claim MoE outperforms dense overstated; dense better or equal on several tasks
No seeds, variances or significance tests
Comparison confounded by extra SFT/DPO for MoE; dense post-training undescribed
Missing baselines: union-data model, model soup, MergeKit/Mergoo merging
'6B activated parameters' figure not derived; parameter counts missing
No systems evaluation of build time, memory, throughput or latency
Efficiency benefit unrealised without optimised kernels; BTS memory not quantified
Comparison with MergeKit/Mergoo only qualitative; no feature table
Other MoE tooling (HF, Megatron/DeepSpeed-MoE, Tutel) not discussed; 'previously unavailable' unsupported
Router initialisation, inference expert selection and load-balancing loss unspecified
Visualization claimed valuable for diagnosis but no real case shown
Averaging routing weights crude; no faithfulness analysis of routing
Loose text, confusing Fig. 1 caption, wrong panel references
Introduction mixes loosely related catastrophic-forgetting claims
Related work dwells on MoE history and has odd citation
Code unavailable; tests, documentation, CI, licensing not described
Copying upstream modeling files raises long-term maintenance concerns
LoRA settings partial; DPO data and hyperparameters absent
Unclear whether Table 1 reproduction succeeds; more replication experiments needed
Motivation weak: no need shown beyond DeepSpeed-MoE, FairScale, Megatron
Contribution is engineering integration without scientific innovation
Experiments only small multilingual code-switching; no comparison to Mixtral, DeepSeekMoE, Switch
No large-scale or cross-domain results
No measurement of efficiency, scalability or convergence stability
Merging compute cost and compatibility issues (tokenizer, architecture) not discussed
Small gains make practical benefit marginal
No comparison with model-merging frameworks (AdapterFusion, LoRAHub, ModelSoup)
Visualization analyses descriptive; no routing entropy or utilization statistics
Usefulness of supporting BTX/BTS doubtful; few frontier models use them
No research-focused efficiency optimization for MoE
Many existing codebases already provide MoE training and visualization
Unclear how to integrate with other training codebases like Megatron
Training/inference efficiency versus Megatron and other frameworks unknown
Usability unverifiable; 'proven valuable' scenarios not described
No reimplementation of original BTX/BTS experiments with configs and code
'Reimplementation' matches original exactly; likely not independent evidence of usability
No comprehensive list of configuration options
No example adapter file for adding new MoE variant
